because: Counterexample (hunt round 2, 2026-10-10): a claim id is the hash of its bytes, so a detection byte-identical to a claim retracted in the same millisecond (same target, reason and end: a source TTL, or a permanent policy) got the retracted id. It was reported as a new, applied claim and its resend became a duplicate, yet it was never in force. Fix: issue_own moves such a claim a millisecond later until its id is free.
evidence_text: `a_detection_refused_at_capacity_leaves_no_event_and_no_strike` (mutations "remember the event first" and "count the strike first" each fail it), `a_detection_after_a_same_instant_retraction_is_enforced`, `a_permanent_redetection_after_a_same_instant_retraction_is_enforced`
statement: A detection checks its event id, adds or merges the claim, then records the event, under one table lock. A resend of an event acted on within EVENT_MEMORY is a duplicate. A refused detection (here: the known-claims cap) records no event and counts no strike: a resend after capacity frees is decided afresh, and the next block of that target gets the TTL of its first strike.
